explanation:
The input is split by full-height divider columns into panels of equal size. Each output has the size of one panel. I looked at the panels with an inspect call, and they read like snapshots of an animation. Each one shows a single multi-cell **shape** plus scattered **single dots**, and the dots disappear from panel to panel.

**What the shape is doing.** The shape is mirror-symmetric about one axis, so it has a **tip** pointing in one direction. It travels in straight lines and eats dots:

- From its tip, it moves straight ahead to the nearest dot in that direction. It is re-stamped so its tip sits on that dot, and the dot is eaten.
- If no dot lies straight ahead, it turns left or right towards a direction that has a dot in line, rotates the shape to face that way, and continues.
- When no dot lies ahead or to either side, it stops. The output is the panel with only the shape at its final position and orientation.

**Checking this against the pairs:**

- **Pair 2:** The upward T has its tip at (5,1). It goes up to (1,1), right to (1,4), down to (4,4), then down to (6,4). The last two match the 4th panel and the output: tip on (6,4), pointing down.
- **Pair 1:** The "<" has its tip at (2,5). It goes left to (2,3), down to (5,3) (panel 2 shows the V there, pointing down), right to (5,6), down to (8,6) (panel 3), left to (8,1), then up to (1,1). The output is the V pointing up with its tip at (1,1).
- **Pair 3:** The shape has its tip at (2,3), pointing right. It visits (2,6), (2,10), (5,10), then left to (5,7) and (5,4) (panel 2), then (5,2), (9,2), (9,5), and up through (7,5) to (0,5). The output shape points up with its tip at (0,5).

The intermediate panels match the path, so only the **first panel** is needed: run the walk to the end.

**Finding the tip in code.** For each of the 4 directions, the candidate tip is the shape's extreme cell in that direction. That cell must be unique, and the shape must be mirror-symmetric about the line through it in that direction. This identifies the tip uniquely in all three pairs and in the test.

**Rotating the shape.** Each cell is stored as an offset from the tip, split into a forward component along the direction and a sideways component. The cell is rebuilt the same way for the new direction.

**Test input.** There are no dividers, so the whole 15×15 grid is the single panel. The shape's tip is at (5,7), pointing up. The walk goes up to (1,7), right to (1,12), down to (3,12), left through (3,9) to (3,3), down to (8,3), left to (8,1), down to (13,1), then right through (13,6) to (13,10). It ends pointing right with its tip at (13,10).

Two dots, (6,4) and (6,10), are never reached. Every train output contains only the shape, so I clear all remaining dots. This is an assumption: no train pair has a dot that goes uneaten, so they don't show whether leftover dots should stay.
